title: SDK auth ergonomics: ephemeral SSO token flow, key rotation patterns, and secure local secret guidance
creator: Maya Li
description: Define SDK-level guidance, implementation patterns, and example snippets for: (1) short-lived API keys and automated rotation, (2) enterprise SSO token issuance and refresh ergonomics, (3) local secret handling best practices (dev workstations / CI), and (4) retry semantics and streaming edge-cases for auth failures. Outputs: design doc, example code in Python/TS/Go included in SDK repo, test plan, and a security review checklist.
acceptance_criteria: A design doc describing the recommended token lifetimes, refresh flows, and rotation API surfaces is published to Confluence
SDKs (python, typescript, go) include example helper utilities for (a) automated key rotation polling, (b) ephemeral SSO exchange, and (c) ephemeral credential caching + secure zero-disk fallback
Unit and integration tests exercise rotation edge cases and token-refresh race conditions in CI
Security team signs off on the secrets handling guidance and the documented KMS/HSM integration approach
Documentation in SDK README demonstrates best-practice env var names, platform endpoints, and a migration path for customers with long-lived keys
notes: We will prefer short-lived credentials (<=1h) for interactive flows and 24h for machine-to-machine where rotation automation is available
Trade-off: very short token lifetimes increase rotation traffic and slightly more latency during refresh; mitigated via local in-memory caching and jittered background refresh
Design decision: do NOT bake private key material into SDKs. Flow should support platform-side rotation endpoints and customer-managed KMS for Private deployments
For SSO enterprise flows, use OIDC authorization_code + token exchange to produce an ephemeral platform token; SDKs should expose a simple ExchangeSSOToken helper
Streaming note: streaming responses must detect token expiry mid-stream and surface a clear error code (auth_expired) so apps can retry with resumed context if supported by the runtime
tasks: Draft Confluence design doc (link will be added to attachments)
Implement helper module in python sdk: rotate_helpers.py with polling + safe-write to disk and memory-only fallback
Add example in typescript sdk showing SSO exchange using fetch + automatic refresh middleware
Add example in go sdk demonstrating context-aware token injection and exponential-backoff on 401s
Write integration tests to simulate token expiry during streaming and verify retry/resume behavior
Schedule security review with Security team and apply feedback
Create a lightweight migration guide for customers using long-lived API keys
comments: 2026-03-05 - Maya Li: Initial ticket created after postmortem call with platform team. Root cause for two incidents was stale long-lived keys used in CI. Proposed to standardize ephemeral tokens + rotation helpers.

2026-03-06 - Devon Harper: Spike completed for python rotation helper. Implemented background refresh with leader election (file lock) to avoid thundering herd in multi-process dev setups. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/421

2026-03-07 - Security (Nina Alvarez): Requested explicit guidance for local dev: prefer OS keychain (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / libsecret) and avoid committing .env. Also requested KMS integration notes for Private customers.
2026-03-08 - Design review (Jon Park): Suggested adding a short CLI utility to bootstrap ephemeral creds for devs (redwood auth login) and to support SSO headless flows for CI runners.

2026-03-09 - Devon Harper: Added TypeScript middleware prototype that injects tokens and transparently performs refresh on 401 with single inflight refresh using a promise lock pattern. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/434

2026-03-11 - QA (Rita Gomez): Reported an edge case where token refresh during active streaming produced duplicate events. Investigating whether runtime should support resumable streams or SDK must buffer outbound state to resume. Filed follow-up ENG-30258
2026-03-12 - Maya Li: Consolidated security feedback and updated acceptance criteria. Security review scheduled for 2026-03-18. Added migration guidance bullet to README draft.
